task.description:
WF-03 documentation update for run WF03-ISS0106-20260821. TWO tasks. Note that ISSUE-FIXER is concurrently editing files under docs/issues/ for this same run -- do NOT touch anything in that directory, it is not yours this step.

**TASK 1 -- add an entry to docs/anti-patterns.md.** This run produced a finding that meets that file's own bar (CLAUDE.md: 'add to it when you find a mistake worth not repeating'), and it is a NEW INSTANCE OF AN EXISTING CLASS rather than a new class -- so read the existing entry 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source' first and decide, on the evidence, whether this belongs as an update appended to that entry or as its own new entry. Either is acceptable; state your reasoning in the handoff. What happened:

  ISS-0106 was filed with a root cause stated as 'ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, not inferred)' -- toolchain drift, this host running Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 against a .tool-versions pin of 1.18.3-otp-27. That framing was wrong for half the issue, and the framing shaped everything downstream: the issue's own proposed resolution (a) was 'install the pinned toolchain and confirm both checks go green with NO FILE CHANGES AT ALL, which would prove the files are correct and only the host was wrong.' This run ran that check -- and the premise failed. Under the pinned Elixir 1.18.3/OTP 27, in a throwaway container against the same tree, `mix format --check-formatted` fails on the SAME four files with character-for-character identical diffs, including the heredoc escape ISS-0106 attributed specifically to a formatter behaviour change between versions. Three of the four diffs are ordinary line-length wraps, measured at 99-102 characters against a formatter default line length of 98 that .formatter.exs never overrides -- no Elixir version has ever accepted them. The files were made unformatted by three commits that merged on 2026-08-20, each verified format-clean at its parent commit and unformatted at itself. Only the second symptom (14 struct-update warnings) was genuine version drift, and that one was confirmed cleanly: 14 warnings under 1.20.3, zero under 1.18.3, same tree.

  The instructive parts, which are what make this worth recording rather than just a wrong guess:
  (i) The refuting check was AVAILABLE THE WHOLE TIME and cost one container run. Docker was on the host, and docs/anti-patterns.md already documented the throwaway-elixir-container recipe. Nobody had run the pinned toolchain before asserting what it would do.
  (ii) The wrong attribution was PLAUSIBLE and CONFIDENTLY WORDED, and a real drift did exist alongside it -- which is what made it survive. Half the diagnosis was right, and the correct half lent credibility to the incorrect half.
  (iii) A version-attributed formatting failure is CHEAP TO REFUTE WITHOUT ANY TOOLCHAIN AT ALL: measure the line lengths. A line over the formatter's default 98 characters is unformatted under every version that has ever had a formatter. That check needs no container, no install, and no second host.
  (iv) The consequence of believing it was concrete rather than theoretical: it deferred a real defect as an environment problem, and ISS-0106 itself predicted this consequence in the abstract while being an instance of it.

  Write the entry in the file's established format -- what happened, why it is wrong for this project specifically, and the correct alternative. Follow the tone and structure of the existing entries; several of them include a 'why this is easy to miss' paragraph, which fits this finding well. Cite concrete evidence (commit shas 91d7e25 / cb43cc2 / a7fa87b, the measured line lengths, the container result) rather than describing it abstractly -- the file's existing entries are specific, and a vague entry would be the thing it warns against.

  Do NOT write an entry about the gate-discipline finding (three runs merging past a red format gate). That is already filed as ISS-0110 / GH#363 / queue task 177 and is deliberately a separate, unresolved investigation -- writing its conclusions into anti-patterns.md now would pre-empt a question that issue exists to answer.

**TASK 2 -- append the run's events to docs/status/requirement_status.yaml.** READ THE FILE IN FULL FIRST and preserve its established schema exactly. This file is APPEND-ONLY: an agent has previously rewritten it from scratch with different field names and silently destroyed prior history, and that incident is itself recorded in docs/anti-patterns.md. Append, never rewrite. Your diff on this file must show insertions and ZERO deletions. Record the ISS-0106 resolution consistent with how other WF-03 issue-resolution runs are recorded in that file -- match the existing convention rather than inventing a shape for it.

Context for both tasks: ISS-0106's two symptoms are fixed and verified by the gate itself -- `mix letflow.check` step 2 (format) and step 3 (compile --warnings-as-errors) both now PASS. The alias still exits 1 at step 4 for an unrelated, already-tracked reason (ISS-0107 / GH#357, Windows fake-mix self-recursion). Do not describe the gate as green.
acceptance_criteria: docs/anti-patterns.md carries the new content, either as its own entry or as an update to the existing 'Inheriting a claim from a record' entry, with the choice reasoned in your handoff

The new content cites concrete measured evidence -- the three commit shas, the measured line lengths versus the 98-character default, and the container result showing the pinned toolchain rejects the same four files -- rather than describing the finding abstractly

The new content states the cheap general refutation (a line over 98 characters is unformatted under every formatter version, measurable with no toolchain at all) as the correct alternative, since that is the transferable lesson
It does NOT pre-empt ISS-0110's open question about how three runs merged past a red gate
docs/anti-patterns.md's existing entries are untouched except for any deliberate append to the one named above -- verify with git diff that your change is additive
docs/status/requirement_status.yaml has the run's event(s) APPENDED in the file's existing schema, and `git diff --numstat` on that file shows ZERO deletions. Quote that numstat output
No file outside docs/anti-patterns.md, docs/status/requirement_status.yaml and your own handoff is modified -- in particular nothing under docs/issues/, which ISSUE-FIXER is editing concurrently

result.summary:
Both tasks done. Two files written, both additive, both verified with git diff --numstat.

===== TASK 1 -- docs/anti-patterns.md =====

CHOICE, AND THE REASONING THE HANDOFF ASKED FOR: a NEW ENTRY, plus a three-line cross-reference appended to the existing 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source' entry pointing forward to it. New entry title: 'Attributing a failure to toolchain drift without ever running the pinned toolchain'.

Why new rather than an append, decided on the evidence rather than by preference:
(1) The existing entry is a CLOSED NARRATIVE with a specific frame -- its own first line is 'Occurred three times in one session (WF01-REQ109-20260819), each time compounding the last', and its body is a numbered 1/2/3 chain in which each instance inherits the previous one's frame. This finding is from a different run two days later and does not compound those three; grafting it in as a '4.' would falsify the entry's own thesis about compounding within one session.
(2) The transferable lesson is DIFFERENT IN KIND, not just a fourth data point. The existing entry's correct-alternative list is about re-deriving records generally (verify a premise before scoping, don't derive list and pattern from each other, scope greps to code, treat 'unreachable' as expiring, supersede rather than overwrite). None of those catches this one. What catches this one is a domain-specific test the general entry has no place for: measure the offending lines against the formatter's configured line_length. An entry a reader can act on in one command deserves its own heading rather than being the sixth bullet of a general one.
(3) The file already has precedent for BOTH shapes, so this was a real choice rather than a default. It appends when the new instance is the same mechanism recurring under the same conditions ('Two branches picking the same module name' has an appended final paragraph for a second collision), and it splits when the recurrence has its own procedure ('ISS-NNNN collisions keep recurring because documenting the hazard doesn't reserve the number' is a separate entry from the ISS-NNNN entry above it, precisely because the fix is different). This is the second shape.
(4) Discoverability was the one real argument for appending, and the cross-reference solves it without the costs above: a reader who lands on the general entry is told a fourth instance exists and where, and the new entry closes by naming the general entry as its parent class.

EVIDENCE CITED CONCRETELY, not abstractly (AC2): the three commit shas with their issue/PR numbers (91d7e25 = ISS-0080/GH#301, cb43cc2 = ISS-0078/GH#299 PR#347, a7fa87b = GH#298 PR#349, all merged 2026-08-20) and the per-file before/after method that established them (`git show <rev>:<path> | mix format --check-formatted -`, all four exit 0 at parent, exit 1 at the commit); the measured 99-102 characters against the formatter's default line_length of 98 that .formatter.exs never overrides; the container result named by image tag (elixir:1.18.3-otp-27, repo mounted read-only, tree copied to /work) with the four failing paths and their exact line numbers (pin_resolver.ex:541, variable_merge.ex:92,98, pin_resolver_test.exs:239,322, pin_rebind_test.exs:516) and the explicit note that the heredoc-escape diff ISS-0106 attributed to a version change is present under the pin too; and the compile counter-measurement (14 warnings under 1.20.3/OTP 29, zero under 1.18.3/OTP 27, identical tree).

THE CHEAP GENERAL REFUTATION IS STATED AS THE CORRECT ALTERNATIVE (AC3): the entry states in italics that a line over 98 characters is unformatted under every Elixir version that has ever had a formatter, gives the one-command awk check that measures it, and states explicitly that it needs no container, no install, no second host and no network -- then generalises it to 'before attributing a formatting failure to a version, measure the diff against the configured line_length'. Three further procedural bullets follow: never write ROOT CAUSE (confirmed) for a toolchain you have not run; re-derive each symptom's attribution separately when they merely share a failing command; run the check the issue itself proposes before proposing anything downstream of it.

ISS-0110 NOT PRE-EMPTED (AC4): the entry states the three commits as measured fact because that is the evidence for the misattribution, then says in one sentence that WHY those runs' format gates did not stop them 'is a separate, still-open question -- tracked as ISS-0110/GH#363, deliberately not answered here'. No conclusion about gate discipline, agent behaviour, or how the merges happened appears anywhere in the entry. Nothing under docs/issues/ was read or written by me.

ADDITIVITY VERIFIED (AC5): `git diff --numstat docs/anti-patterns.md` -> `80\t0\tdocs/anti-patterns.md`. 80 insertions, ZERO deletions. Every pre-existing entry is byte-identical; the only change inside an existing entry is the three-line cross-reference paragraph appended after the final bullet of the 'Inheriting a claim' entry, which is the deliberate append this handoff authorised.

===== TASK 2 -- docs/status/requirement_status.yaml =====

READ IN FULL FIRST, as instructed. The file is 349.6KB / 5723 lines and exceeded the read tool's single-call limit, so it was read via head/tail plus targeted extraction of every distinct `req:` value and every structurally distinct entry shape -- specifically: the 17-line header comment block that states the schema, the first entries, the last entries, all 30 `req: SCOPE-CHANGE` entries' identifiers with three read in full, and the full set of distinct req identifiers (`grep '^  - req: ' | sort -u`). Schema confirmed as exactly req/event/agent/at/note, five keys, note as a `>` folded block.

CONVENTION MATCHED RATHER THAN INVENTED, which required a decision: there is NO precedent anywhere in 5723 lines for a `req: ISS-NNNN` entry. The distinct req values are REQ-001..REQ-066, REQ-082, REQ-101..REQ-112, and SCOPE-CHANGE -- nothing else. WF-03 issue-resolution runs that are not attached to a requirement are recorded under `req: SCOPE-CHANGE` with `event: done`, and the note opens by naming the issue and its GitHub number -- e.g. the ISS-0030/GH#89 entry ('Resolved ISS-0030 (GH#89, BLOCKER...)'), the ISS-0019/GH#75 entry, and the ISS-0092/GH#314 entry. I followed that shape exactly: `req: SCOPE-CHANGE`, `event: done`, `agent: DOC-UPDATER`, note opening 'ISS-0106 / GH#354 resolved by run WF03-ISS0106-20260821.' Inventing `req: ISS-0106` would have been a new shape in a file that already has one for this case.

ONE EVENT, not two. A `started` event was considered and deliberately not written: this run's start was 2026-08-21T01:00:16Z and I am appending at 03:39:49Z, so a started event now could only carry either a back-dated timestamp (forbidden -- timestamps come from the clock) or a timestamp that misrepresents when the run started. The SCOPE-CHANGE issue-resolution precedent is single-`done` in every one of the three entries examined, so one event also matches the convention.

TIMESTAMP FROM THE CLOCK: `date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"` -> 2026-08-21T03:39:49Z, read immediately before the append, not from memory or from any handoff field.

CONTENT: the two-root-cause split with the container refutation, the three commit shas, the 99-102 vs 98 measurement, the confirmed 14-vs-0 warning drift and its settling of ISS-0046's UNCONFIRMED note, the three-part fix (A: pin moved to elixir 1.20.3-otp-29 / erlang 29.0.5 plus `mix letflow.check_toolchain` prepended to the check alias; B: four files reformatted; C: 16 struct-update bind sites annotated), the REVIEWER sign-off amending decision 0005, the README.md and backend_developer_guide.md doc updates, and ISS-0110/GH#363/task 177 named as separate and still open.

GATE STATE NOT DESCRIBED AS GREEN, per the handoff's explicit instruction: the note says in terms 'Gate state, and it is NOT green' -- step 2 (format) and step 3 (compile --warnings-as-errors) PASS, and the alias still exits 1 at step 4 for ISS-0107 / GH#357 (Windows fake-mix self-recursion), unrelated and already tracked.

ZERO DELETIONS, QUOTED AS AC6 REQUIRES: `git diff --numstat docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` -> `43\t0\tdocs/status/requirement_status.yaml`. 43 insertions, ZERO deletions. Nothing was rewritten; the 43 lines are appended after the existing final line. Independently re-verified by parsing: `yaml.safe_load` gives 182 history entries (181 before + 1), keys of the last entry are exactly ['req','event','agent','at','note'], and the file still parses as valid YAML.

ENCODING NOTE, handled rather than left as a latent defect: both files are CRLF in the working copy (core.autocrlf=true; .gitattributes forces LF for *.ex/*.exs only, per ISS-0008). My heredoc appends wrote LF, which git normalised correctly but left the working copy with mixed endings. I converted both files' line endings back to uniform CRLF and re-ran numstat afterward to confirm the conversion introduced no deletions -- still 80/0 and 43/0.

===== SCOPE (AC7) =====

`git status --short` shows my three files (docs/anti-patterns.md, docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, handoffs/WF03-ISS0106-20260821/step-05b-doc-update.json) plus ISSUE-FIXER's and ORCH's concurrent work, which I did not touch: docs/issues/ISS-0106.yaml and docs/issues/ISS-0110.yaml (ISSUE-FIXER's, running concurrently -- not read, not written), and handoffs/orchestrator.log and handoffs/registry.json (ORCH's, untouched per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md sections 4 and 7). No source file, test, or decision record was modified. My commit stages only my own three paths by name, never `git add -A`.

issues.description: docs/status/requirement_status.yaml is 349.6KB / 5723 lines and now exceeds the read tool's 256KB single-call limit, so no agent can any longer follow this file's own instruction to 'read it in full first' with one read. That instruction is the stated safeguard against the rewrite incident recorded in docs/anti-patterns.md's 'Overwriting docs/status/requirement_status.yaml instead of appending' entry, and a safeguard that can no longer be executed as written is one an agent will improvise around -- which is how the original incident happened. I worked around it here by reading the header/schema block, both ends, and every structurally distinct entry shape, but that is a technique, not an instruction the file gives. Worth either splitting the file by period (e.g. requirement_status-2026-08.yaml with an index) or rewriting the header's guidance to prescribe the scoped-read technique explicitly. Not fixed by this run: the file's own header is prior art that predates this handoff's scope and changing it is a convention change, not a bookkeeping append.

This file's header block documents the schema as req/event/agent/at/note and says 'Append one entry per event', but says nothing about what goes in `req` for work that is not a requirement. The answer is established purely by 30 precedent entries using `req: SCOPE-CHANGE` for issue resolutions and scope changes. An agent that reads only the header -- which is what the header invites -- has no way to know that, and inventing `req: ISS-0106` would look entirely reasonable. One sentence in the header naming SCOPE-CHANGE as the identifier for non-requirement events would close it. Same reasoning as above for why I did not make the change myself.
